video_title: Gold & Silver Stocks Now A Screaming Buy? | Jeff Clark's Top Picks
gist: Jeff Clark (Gold Advisor) argues gold's dip masks bullish internals (record Q3 ETF inflows, central bank and China buying, 93% match to the 1970s bull) and that miners are historically cheap and tiny relative to capital pools; he then lists new stock picks across exploration, resource-builder and developer categories.

insights.claim: Jeff Clark says gold has risen alongside Treasury yields on an annual basis since the end of 2021, an unusual relationship he reads as evidence that large institutions are buying despite a 10-year yield of 5.35% (24-year high), a 2% monthly dollar gain, 3.4% CPI and a Fed hike with ~85% odds of another.
insights.speaker: Jeff Clark
insights.so_what: Gold's strength against hostile rates/dollar suggests the recent drawdown is a dip within an intact uptrend.
insights.quote: gold has been rising with yields since 2022

insights.claim: Central banks remain net gold buyers: Clark cites a monthly add of 39 tonnes (up 70% month on month, double a year earlier), year-to-date purchases on track to exceed 2025, and a World Gold Council survey showing rising intent to increase reserves over 12 months.
insights.speaker: Jeff Clark
insights.so_what: Official-sector demand provides a price-insensitive bid that is strongest on dips.

insights.claim: China has bought gold for 23 consecutive months (24 imminent), holds over $323 billion in gold reserves, and its Q2 2026 purchases accelerated, which Clark reads as dollar diversification.
insights.speaker: Jeff Clark
insights.so_what: Sustained PBoC buying is a structural de-dollarization signal supporting gold floors.

insights.claim: Q3 saw the largest quarterly global gold ETF inflow on record, which Clark highlights because gold ETF flows skew institutional (unlike silver ETFs, mostly retail).
insights.speaker: Jeff Clark
insights.so_what: Record institutional inflows during a price slump signals accumulation under negative headlines.

insights.claim: Clark argues gold has tracked the 1976-1980 bull market with ~93% correlation since the bull began on leap-year day 2024; if the analog holds, gold would roughly double from current levels (about $10,000) within a year to a year and a half after a further flat period.
insights.speaker: Jeff Clark
insights.so_what: A pattern-match forecast; the 'flat for a bit longer' leg implies near-term chop before breakout. He explicitly says he is not predicting it.

insights.claim: Clark argues gold has not truly broken out because relative to the Nasdaq the gold ratio is near all-time lows and has recently cheapened, despite gold having doubled since the bull began.
insights.speaker: Jeff Clark
insights.so_what: Gold looks cheap versus equity risk assets, leaving room for rotation.

themes.theme: Miners are cheap vs gold and tiny vs capital pools

insights.claim: Clark cites a chart showing projected 2026-2028 mining stock valuations as the cheapest on record on price-to-NAV with the highest free-cash-flow yield ever measured, calling mining stocks the cheapest in 50 years.
insights.speaker: Jeff Clark
insights.so_what: Fundamental case for miners rests on record FCF yield at current gold prices.
insights.quote: mining stocks that are the cheapest in 50 years

insights.claim: The HUI gold-miner index relative to gold is no higher than in 2020 and lower than in 2016, 2011, 2003 and far below 1979-80, which Clark says shows miners have not participated in gold's doubling.
insights.speaker: Jeff Clark
insights.so_what: Ratio mean reversion implies miners could outpace the metal if gold holds.

insights.claim: Mining equities are about 2% of global equities, the smallest share in 55 years, with a ~$400 billion industry market cap against $8.5 trillion of global sideline cash and a $127 trillion bond market.
insights.speaker: Jeff Clark
insights.so_what: Tiny market cap means modest allocation shifts from cash/bonds could cause outsized moves in miners.

insights.claim: Clark argues disillusionment with bonds and an underperforming 60/40 portfolio since COVID could push even a small fraction of bond investors into miners, producing a dramatic price impact given the sector's size.
insights.speaker: Jeff Clark
insights.so_what: Capital-flow thesis: reallocation from bonds is a potential catalyst for sector re-rating.

insights.claim: Clark segments mining stocks into pre-discovery, pre-resource, resource builders and developers, each with different risk and catalyst: discovery, inaugural resource, doubling or tripling the resource, and nearing a construction decision.
insights.speaker: Jeff Clark
insights.so_what: Match position size to category risk; lower-risk categories are protected by an existing resource.

insights.claim: Clark says to own resource builders before drilling results land, because positive results make the market buy in anticipation of a larger resource, and the needed growth is a doubling or tripling rather than 10-20%.
insights.speaker: Jeff Clark
insights.so_what: Entry timing ahead of drill news is where the edge lies.

insights.claim: For developers the key question is whether it will become a mine and whether a major would buy it; Clark looks for big, rich, long-life assets in pro-mining jurisdictions near a construction decision, expecting most to be acquired rather than build.
insights.speaker: Jeff Clark
insights.so_what: M&A takeout is the main return path for developers, so asset quality and jurisdiction drive value.

insights.claim: Clark's new pick Bullfrog Gold holds the 'donor hole' between Kinross and AngloGold Ashanti deposits in Nevada; a first drill program starts imminently with assays before year end, and he expects a buyout by either major if it hits.
insights.speaker: Jeff Clark
insights.so_what: Binary exploration catalyst with a natural acquirer; Clark is overweight via private placement.

insights.claim: Sun Come Up Metals holds two copper-gold properties in the Solomon Islands on the same trend as Panguna and a giant gold deposit with over 71 million ounces; assays are imminent, though the jurisdiction is rated high political risk.
insights.speaker: Jeff Clark
insights.so_what: High-risk, near-term assay catalyst in a geologically proven belt.

insights.claim: Aurania Metals (Ecuador gold-copper) has reported results such as 905 m of 0.6% gold and 0.12% copper, and Clark sees fair value of at least C$2 with the stock below it; Ecuador's newly mining-friendly stance is a risk he will exit on if it reverses.
insights.speaker: Jeff Clark
insights.so_what: Jurisdiction improvement plus drill results; political risk at next election is the watch item.

insights.claim: Cascadia Minerals (Yukon copper-gold) has a resource but historical drilling left deeper higher-grade sulfide untested; Clark expects a significant re-rating if drilling continues to succeed.
insights.speaker: Jeff Clark
insights.so_what: Re-rating thesis rests on deeper high-grade zones.

insights.claim: Gatty Copper just began its first significant drill campaign in 30 years next to the Highland Valley Copper mine, with hits like 184 m of 0.37% copper and 150 m of 0.7%; Clark thinks Highland's falling head grade makes it a likely acquirer.
insights.speaker: Jeff Clark
insights.so_what: Strategic fit with a neighbouring declining-grade mine supports takeout logic.

insights.claim: Rackla Metals is drilling a high-grade tungsten project for the first time in 44 years, aiming to confirm and expand a historical resource; Clark is buying on the stock's weakness.
insights.speaker: Jeff Clark
insights.so_what: Critical-metal exposure with a historical resource to validate.

insights.claim: Sunpeak Metals is an early mover in Saudi Arabia, which Clark says has become very pro-mining and supportive of foreign miners; the company has a discovery and is drilling multiple projects.
insights.speaker: Jeff Clark
insights.so_what: Jurisdictional shift in Saudi Arabia is an under-appreciated tailwind for early-mover juniors.

insights.claim: Pacifica Silver, a silver explorer near Durango, Mexico, is backed by First Majestic, Silvercorp, Vizsla Silver and Eric Sprott; Clark visited the project, calls it one of his biggest 2025 investments and sees the recent silver-driven dip as an entry point.
insights.speaker: Jeff Clark
insights.so_what: Strategic silver-company investors validate the project; stock is down with silver.

insights.claim: A2 Gold is one of few Nevada juniors able to prove a multi-million ounce deposit; Clark thinks the next resource could be 2-3 million ounces, backed by Kinross and Eric Sprott, and the stock is near one- to two-year lows after the gold sell-off.
insights.speaker: Jeff Clark
insights.so_what: Resource expansion surprise plus majors seeking ounces makes it a takeout candidate at a depressed price.

insights.claim: Banyan Gold has 8.6 million ounces in the Yukon next to Hecla with infrastructure and permitting, and Clark calls it a top buyout candidate but suggests waiting for a dip after its past-year run.
insights.speaker: Jeff Clark
insights.so_what: Large resource plus infrastructure; entry-timing advice is to buy weakness.

insights.claim: Mako Mining and Silver consolidated a legendary Nevada gold-silver district under one owner, has two drill programs running, and is a new overweight pick for Clark.
insights.speaker: Jeff Clark
insights.so_what: District consolidation makes the asset more attractive to acquirers.

insights.claim: Newcore Gold in Ghana looks undervalued on NAV with a PEA coming; Clark calculates Ghana's new royalty regime adds about $150/oz to all-in sustaining cost, which he views as not a deal-killer in the top-ranked pro-mining African jurisdiction.
insights.speaker: Jeff Clark
insights.so_what: Resource-nationalism cost is quantifiable and modest; eventual producer buyout expected.

insights.claim: Grand Portage's Herbert Gold project in Alaska was accepted as a US fast-track covered project; its PEA shows $721 million after-tax NPV at $3,200 gold (near $1 billion at $4,000) versus a market cap of about $55 million, with first pour not before 2030-31.
insights.speaker: Jeff Clark
insights.so_what: Huge NPV-to-market-cap gap should narrow with de-risking or a buyout, but timeline is long.

insights.claim: Clark discloses owning all the picks, many of which are overweight or acquired via private placements and sit behind his newsletter paywall, so the recommendations carry promotional bias.
insights.speaker: Jeff Clark
insights.so_what: Treat the picks as marketing-adjacent starting points for diligence, not independent research.
